rmai

Use mai, the compiled statistical computing language from Brendan McArdle’s 2018 University of Auckland PhD thesis, from R.

mai reads a lot like R, but compiles loops and function calls to fast bytecode. rmai builds the mai executable, passes R data to it and brings results back, and lets you write {mai} chunks in R Markdown and Quarto.

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mai-lib/rmai")
rmai::mai_install()        # download and build mai (Linux: needs gcc, bison, m4, readline, valgrind headers)

Evaluate mai code on R data 

library(rmai)
x <- runif(1e6)

mai_eval("sum(sqrt(x))", x = x)

mai_eval(
  "var n = length(x), s = 0.0
   for(int i = 1; i <= n; i = i + 1) s = s + x[i] * x[i]
   s",
  x = x
)

mai_eval("m * 10.0", m = matrix(as.double(1:6), 2))

Named arguments become const globals in mai. Double, integer and logical vectors, matrices and arrays go in and come back exactly, NA included.

Results as ALTREP vectors

With .altrep = TRUE (or options(rmai.altrep = TRUE)), a vector or array result is not read into R. It stays in mai’s output, mapped into memory, and R gets an ALTREP vector over it that behaves as an ordinary vector, matrix or array.

r <- mai_eval("m * 2.0", m = matrix(runif(1e6), 1000), .altrep = TRUE)
r[10, 1:5]          # reads 5 values, not a million
mai_vec_info(r)     # what R has asked for: elt, region, dataptr, array_subset

Integers are used in place. Doubles are too, once mai’s NA values are rewritten as R’s on the first full data request. Logicals are converted to R’s layout on the first full data request, since mai stores them in one byte.

On stock R, r[i, j, k] asks for one element at a time. On an R with the proposed Extract_array_subset ALTREP method (the array-subset variant in mdsumner/r-variants), rmai answers it in one call, and mai_has_array_subset() is TRUE. tools/r-variants-array-subset.sh runs the ALTREP tests in that image.

Once rmai runs mai as a library rather than a separate process, the same vectors can point at mai’s memory directly.

Run scripts and code 

mai_run("print(sum(1:100))")
mai_source("analysis.mai")

Compare with R 

mai_compare(
  "const fib = function(n) if(n <= 2) 1 else fib(n - 2) + fib(n - 1)
   const run = function() fib(25)",
  "fib <- function(n) if (n <= 2) 1 else fib(n - 2) + fib(n - 1)
   run <- function() fib(25)"
)

mai chunks in R Markdown and Quarto

Loading rmai registers a mai knitr engine:

```{r}
library(rmai)
```

```{mai, helpers}
const sq = function(double x) : double x * x
```

```{mai, mai.include = "helpers"}
print(sq(1.5))
```

Each chunk runs in a fresh mai process; mai.include names earlier chunks to run first.

Finding the executable

mai_path() looks at options(rmai.path), then MAI_PATH, then the copy installed by mai_install(), then mai on the PATH.

Read before writing much mai

mai is not R. See Differences from R: for example 7 / 2 is 3, and assigning to an undeclared variable inside a function sets a global.
